note: One entry per claim. The layer is decided by what carries the capability, and the gate (scripts/check_layer_separation.py) rejects a claim whose module marker, path or evidence contradicts it.

claims.claim: A fact taught in conversation is recalled: same wording, a taught relation synonym, an English question, a correction, and 12 unrelated turns later.

evidence.method: Invented entities (absent from every corpus); cold -> teach -> same wording -> English -> unseen wording -> correction -> retention -> composition; per-turn answer source recorded.

result.value: recall 7/7 on every stage; cold 7/7 abstain; answers attributed with source=memory

claims.claim: The native engine (GARDEN) learns a fact from dialogue, i.e. the capability survives deletion of the text.

evidence.method: Teach 3 invented facts through the production learner (learn_from_interaction); ask; keep only the SNN checkpoint; ask again. No pipeline, router or memory layer involved.

result.value: cold 0%, taught 0%, after source deletion 0%; the objects are kept verbatim in dictionary.json and the learned pair is (statement -> canned reply)

claims.claim: Curated factual recall of public propositions, with a source.

evidence.method: Native bench: knowledge (15 items, keyword match) and knowledge_mc (40 items).

claims.claim: Extractive answers from an offline public corpus (Simple English Wikipedia, FTS5).

evidence.method: Same knowledge suite; the reader abstains when no retrieved sentence shares two content words with the question (the question's type word is no longer required inside the sentence — that filter discarded the answer sentences; type safety is enforced only in the definition-shaped entity path).

result.value: ablation 2026-10-24: full 8/15 vs curated-only 5/15 vs knowledge-off 0/15 — the layer contributes +3 answers on top of the curated store and abstains on the rest

claims.claim: Chooses a destination and a surface form; it is not a source of facts or of capability.

evidence.method: Per-turn source distribution only; the probe never treats a route as a correctness claim.

result.value: recorded so routing/templates can never be presented as knowledge or learning

claims.claim: A trained core carries a token string across a turn boundary inside its state and generation reads it back: exact match is 0.995 on names and values never seen in training, while zeroing the state or skipping the teaching turn collapses it to 0.000. It is a *mechanism* (how to copy through the state), not knowledge or language: the name selects nothing (wrong_name 0.994).

evidence.method: Teach `remember <name> = <value> .` (no loss) -> al_step(120 s) -> ask `<name> ?` -> generate `<value> .`; the value never appears in turn 2's input. Train/dev/held-out values are disjoint by construction and the leak check is mechanical. Controls: zero_state (same state object, same weights, same prompt, only `h` zeroed), cold (teaching turn skipped; same questions), wrong_name (teach A, ask an untaught B). source_deleted: no evaluation reads the training data or any text store at all - the only artifact is the checkpoint - and deleting the carried state removes the capability, so what remains is a weight-level mechanism rather than a stored string.

result.value: seed 20261114, 60 epochs: held-out exact 0.995 (3,000), dev 0.994; zero-state 0.000, cold 0.000; checkpoint reload reproduces 0.995/0.000. Limits: wrong_name 0.994 (single-slot carry, no keyed lookup), no-al_step 0.003 (not gap-invariant), closed CV alphabet (not language), not wired into production.

claims.claim: The same trained core holds two taught bindings in its state at once and the query selects which one to answer.

evidence.method: Two teaching turns (`ai_step` + `al_step(120 s)` each), then one query naming either taught key, then generate that key's value; the value never appears in the query turn. Round 7 (the registered structural change) added `SlotMemoryCore`: the same GRU plus four gate-written, attention-read slots, 134,124 params, same splits (identical digests). Evaluation reads only the checkpoint - no training text and no value store. `source_deleted` stays true: the only artifact is the checkpoint, and ablating the store removes the capability from the model rather than hiding the answer. Controls: same-parameter GRU (C3, 136,821 params), the same arm with the store ablated (C2), zero-every-state-tensor, zero-h-only, zero-store-only, cold (teaching turns skipped, same questions), `wrong_name` (teach two keys, ask a third).

result.value: Round 7 (seed 20261115, 100 epochs, xpu): `slots` dev 0.0007 / held-out 0.0000, `other_value_rate` 0.0000, i.e. it does not emit a taught value at all. Bars B1 0.60 / B2 0.30. The store is not the missing piece: linear readouts of the addressed content decode both taught values at 0.589/0.593 characters (chance 0.1333; full exact 0.008/0.010 vs chance 2.4e-6). Selection is: `distinct_read_slot_rate` 0.0000/0.0003, `read_cosine_between_asks` 0.9998, `attention_max_prob_mean` 0.97 - both questions read the same slot, confidently. Worse, the store actively hurts decoding: the same arm with the store ablated scores 0.1233 held-out (B7 gap is -0.1233, not +0.20). B8 passes (matched-parameter GRU 0.1557 < 0.30), so parameters are not the explanation. Earlier rounds: single-binding carry passes (0.995), two bindings over one 128-d state fails (0.0033/0.0100), wider `h` does not fix it. Reading: storage works, addressing by a global learned query collapses to a constant position, and the read-into-controller wiring breaks the decoder - the next variable is the addressing signal (per-turn keys), not capacity, width, or epochs.

claims.claim: The same trained core, started from the stage-L byte carrier, reads an eleven-turn testimony and names the person whose value falls inside the theft window.

evidence.method: Corpus is the same generator call as stage L (seed 20261113, 1000 sessions, 0.2 held out; both digests checked against §49.3 before training): 800 train / 200 held-out, eleven turns each, no turn holds the answer (every naming turn is a roll call, evidence turns name nobody, the first evidence row is retracted later). Each session is fed turn by turn through `ai_step`, with `al_step(turn['dt_s'])` between turns, on the same `CoreState` v1; the target is only the culprit's name bytes plus a newline. Every target - full, pre-correction prefix, and each ablation - comes from the generator's `derive()`, not from the oracle field. Start point is the stage-L checkpoint pinned by file sha256 and trained weights hash; 124,611 params, seed 20261118, lr 5e-4, 20 epochs / 2,000 steps, no early stopping. Evaluation reads only the checkpoint and the turn text. A separate format-only arm trains the same text with a random *other* actor as the answer and must stay at chance; the scored arm refuses to start until that report exists and matches the held-out digest. Gates: held-out free exact and 12-way sequence-likelihood ranking (Wilson lower bound must beat the strongest surface baseline's upper bound, 0.2500; chance 0.1591), a state-reset arm, retraction flip on the 98 sessions where the pre-correction prefix has a unique answer, and own-answer share. `source_deleted` is true in the sense the registry asks for: the checkpoint is the only artifact - no answer table, no retrieval store, no per-session lookup - and the held-out sessions were never trained on.

result.value: Stage P (seed 20261118, 20 epochs, xpu, 3,200.6 s): held-out free exact 0.0850 (17/200), ranking 0.1650, against chance 0.1591 and a surface-baseline upper bound of 0.2500; train-split exact 0.1150, so the instrument gate G3 fails - the carrier cannot fit 2,000 steps of training data. G4/G5 (beat the strongest surface baseline), G6 (retraction), G7 (state), G9 (not one constant answer) fail. The format-only control behaves as a null: exact 0.0650, ranking 0.1550, one constant name. The scored arm collapses the same way: one distinct prediction (`Kevin`, share 1.0) for all 200 sessions, and `full`, `reset` (state zeroed before the question) and `skip_al` produce byte-identical predictions (0.0850/0.1650 each). That last equality is the diagnostic, not the score: the state built from the first ten turns contributes nothing to the answer. Per §49.7 the honest reading is the instrument-ceiling branch - no claim about reasoning can be made from this run. §49.16 then measured why: the answer gradient shrinks ~1.13e-03x per turn backwards, so turns 0-7 get no effective update under Adam(eps=1e-8). Stage Q (§50) changed only that path (auxiliary readout at every turn boundary, lambda=1.0, no new parameters) and its Q1 calibration also failed: 32 training sessions, 100 epochs, train exact 0.1562 (5/32, exactly the constant `David`'s marginal) against the registered 0.90, and the paired lambda=0 diagnostic 0.2188. The auxiliary term does reach every turn (a contract test pins |dL/dh| at exactly 0 for turns 0-1 when lambda=0 and > 0 when lambda=1), so the failure sits after credit assignment: the signal arrives and the carrier still cannot fit 32 sessions. Per the registered stop rule the full Q arm was not run and no epochs/lr/width/lambda were adjusted afterwards. Not evidence that path length is unimportant - only that it is not the sole obstacle. §50.13 then probed the other half (linear readout on turn states, fitted on the 800 training sessions, scored on the 200 held-out): the culprit is not decodable at any boundary in any arm (0.055-0.140 against chance 0.0833, inside the shuffled-label null of 0.040-0.105), while the same probe reads the lexical chain at 1.000 on turns 5 and 7 - so the apparatus works and the conclusion simply is not in the state. By turns 9-10 even that chain falls to chance, and the held-out states are nearly collinear (mean pairwise cosine 0.9999, participation ratio 1.06 of 64). The bottleneck is therefore representation, not readout and not credit assignment. Stage R (§51) then removed Q's one nameable defect - supervising boundaries where no answer exists yet - and its R1 calibration also failed: 0.2500 (8/32, top `Ivan` 0.5625) against the registered 0.90, so the pre-registered falsifier (<= 0.30) fired and empty-boundary supervision was ruled out as the cause; the full arm was not run and epochs/lr/width/lambda were not retuned. R1 did not plateau the way Q1 did (main 0.4170 -> 0.3788 -> 0.3609 over epochs 50-100; 2.026 nats/session, only 0.343 below the marginal entropy 2.3691), so the failure point is still the representation. Measured directly: after the last evidence turn the corpus still spends 332 bytes and ~121 `al_step` cell updates (out of ~384 per session) before the answer, and the near-constant dt feature makes those updates contract the state. Stage S (§52) then measured capacity instead of guessing at it, holding the protocol fixed and varying only how many of the first N training sessions must be held at a fixed 400 optimiser steps: N=1 1/1, N=4 4/4 (four distinct names, so the instrument is sound), N=8 7/8 (0.875), N=16 7/16 (0.4375), so the 400-step breakpoint is between 4 and 8. The registered discriminators: N=8 at 4x steps (1,600) passes 8/8 with 7 distinct names in 1,070 s and reproduces the 400-step run's epoch-400 loss exactly (training is deterministic); N=32 at 1,600 steps is 12/32 = 0.375, with main loss stalling near 0.26 and rising to 0.2811 at the end; N=32 at 2x width (hidden 256, 330,563 params, 400 steps) is 10/32 = 0.3125 with `Kevin` predicted 18 times out of 32 and only 4 distinct names. The three 32-session arms are 8/10/12 against a binomial standard error of ~0.077, so steps and width do not differ here, and per the pre-registered rule (2x width still < 0.90 at N* >= 8) the ruling was 'neither'. That ruling was then falsified by the registered §54 check: the ladder held *total* steps fixed, which with batch 8 divides rehearsal per session by N, so N=8 (passed at 1,600 updates/session) and N=32 (given at most 400) were never compared at the same effort. Giving N=32 the same 1,600 updates/session (6,400 steps, 3,969 s) yields 31/32 = 0.9688 with all 12 names predicted and main loss 0.0092 - the same 124,611-parameter carrier fits 32 sessions. So capacity is not the constraint at N=32; the constraint is credit-assignment efficiency: fitting 32 sessions takes 1,600 updates per session, 80x what the 800-session P arm gave (20 updates/session). The report now records `training.updates_per_session` so the two can never be mixed again, and the architecture registration is backed by 'reach the same fit with far fewer updates per session at the 400-updates/session budget where the GRU control is 12/32', not by 'cannot fit'. Stage T (§55) then made the architecture itself the experiment: the same GRU recurrence plus one write at each turn's end and a read that only enters the output head (TurnStoreCore, 168,150 params) reaches 32/32 = 1.0000 at 400 reviews/session (1,600 steps), where the registered GRU control is 12/32 = 0.3750; the same-parameter ablation (memory=False, r = 0, writes disabled) is 16/32 = 0.5000, so T1 (>= 0.90), T2 (<= 0.65 with a >= 0.25 gap), T3 (|0.5000 - 0.3750| = 0.125 <= 0.15) and T4 pass. The ablation is the same function and not merely numerically close: its epoch losses are bit-identical to the GRU's through epoch 25 (the later difference is the head GEMM shape, 192 vs 128 columns, changing float summation order), and its checkpoint's head.weight[:, 128:] has 0 non-zero entries, so the extra columns were never read. This measures the number of updates needed for the same fit (1,600 vs 6,400 steps), not generalisation: §56 registers the same 400 reviews/session on 200 distinct training sessions, graded on the 200 held-out answer tuples. The core score stays 0.00/10. §55 then shortened the credit path (TurnStoreCore, one write per turn read only into the head): 32 sessions at 400 reviews each = 1,600 steps fit 1.0000 (32/32), against 0.5000 for the parameter-matched ablation and 0.3750 for the registered GRU control, with the ablation's loss bit-identical to the GRU through epoch 25 and zero non-zero `head.weight[:, 128:]` entries - i.e. the measured gain is fewer updates to the same fit, not generalisation. §56 (G) tested that: 200 sessions x 400 reviews fits 1.0000 and the held-out stays 0.0850 (Wilson lower bound 0.0537, below the 0.1591 chance), so fitting survives and transfer does not. §57 (H) reallocated the same 10,000 steps to 400 sessions x 200 reviews: fit 0.9125 (365/400), held-out 0.0950, and the prediction lands inside the current session's roster only 0.5350 of the time against a content-free expectation of 0.5457 - so exposure diversity is not the constraint either. §58 (K) probed the state with a linear classifier (no training): it fits the training states (in-sample 0.9725) and the held-out states decode at 0.1100 (Wilson lower bound 0.0738), so the answer is memorised per session and no transferable binding is in the state. §59 (B) tested the representation reading by writing one cache slot per token instead of per turn (TokenCacheCore, 165,956 params): the fit fell to 0.5000, the held-out to 0.0750 and the in-roster rate to 0.5300, falsifying "write granularity is the cause". Per §59.6 the next step is the objective, not more architecture: §60 registers a weighted region loss that restricts each earlier boundary to the session's roster and weights by roster width. The core score stays 0.00/10: fitting is not a correct answer produced by the model on a frozen item.
